usage.title: Interplanetary Magnetic Field (IMF) Components
usage.desc: The MAG (Magnetometer) instrument measures the intensity and vector orientation of the Interplanetary Magnetic Field (IMF) in GSM coordinates:
usage.bt: Total intensity of the magnetic field (nT). Higher values signify severe field disturbance.
usage.bx: Vector component along the Sun-Earth line (sunward/antisunward).
usage.by: Vector component perpendicular to the Earth-Sun line in the ecliptic plane.
usage.bz: Vector component perpendicular to the ecliptic plane. Crucial index for space weather storms.

impacts.title: Bz Alignment & Terrestrial Impacts
impacts.desc: The north-south orientation of the magnetic field (Bz) dictates whether solar wind energy penetrates Earth's magnetosphere:
impacts.north_desc: IMF aligns with Earth's geomagnetic field. Solar particles are deflected safely away.
impacts.south_desc: IMF opposes Earth's field, triggering Magnetic Reconnection that injects energy into the magnetosphere, causing geomagnetic storms and auroras.

details.title: MAG Technical Specifications
details.orbit_val: L1 Lagrangian Point (~1.5 million km upstream of Earth)
details.sensor_val: Dual Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometers on dual deployable booms
details.range_val: ±4 nT to ±65,536 nT (Resolution up to 0.004 nT)
